stories.title: PCB allows Rizwan, Imam to play domestic cricket tournament
summary: It has been reported that Rizwan had asked the PCB for the no-objection certificate to play the Nepal League, but the PCB only allowed him to feature in domestic cricket.
Farah Batool, president of the OGDCL sports department, told Dawn that Imam would play the seventh-round match of the President’s Trophy after receiving the directions from the PCB.
Rizwan, after this case emerged, had requested the PCB to allow him to use the National Cricket Academy which was denied.

stories.title: Indian actor Tiger Shroff remains unhurt in shooting incident in Mumbai
summary: Indian actor Tiger Shroff remained unhurt in a shooting incident in Mumbai’s Juhu area, in which his driver and a bystander sustained injuries, local media reported.

According to the report, Maharashtra Chief Minister and Home Minister Devendra Fadnavis has directed Mumbai Police Commissioner Deven Bharti to investigate the case and take action against the perpetrators.

Local media reported that the responsibility of the attack was claimed in an unverified social media post, which said: “Those in the Mumbai industry who work with Salman Khan and don’t listen to us will meet the same fate.” Authorities have not addressed the post yet.

stories.title: 'Was not sure I'll make it ​out alive': Captain of flydubai flight to Tel Aviv recalls blocking axe blows from co-pilot
summary: The captain of a flydubai flight who was attacked by a co-pilot who intended to crash the plane has described blocking axe blows to the head and screaming for help as he reached for a knob to open the cockpit door.
The suspect, an Omani national, was transferred to the UAE, flydubai’s home country.
Machchhar said he heard the cockpit door opening and screaming “between my colleague and the guy”.

stories.title: Two moments of madness cost Sri Lanka as Pakistan win tri-series opener after Salman Ali Agha century
summary: Only 53 runs stood between them and a flying start in the One-day International tri-series opener against Pakistan after Pavan Rathnayake and Janith Liyanage’s 119-run stand.

Naseem Shah then had Sachindu Colombage caught behind, Eshan Malinga was run out after a mix-up, and Haris cleaned up Asitha Fernando to seal a 37-run win for Pakistan, who had earlier posted 305 thanks to Salman Ali Agha’s third ODI century.
But Sri Lanka’s two costly shots ultimately decided the opener, handing Pakistan a winning start to the tri-series.

stories.title: 2,000 arrested as French unrest spills into second day
summary: French police battled protesters and looters for a second day on Sunday as the country reeled from the violent chaos left by a day of cost-of-living demonstrations in which around 2,000 people were arrested nationwide.
Some 550 people out of 855 arrested in Paris remained in detention from Saturday’s troubles and police stations were struggling to cope, according to the Legal Team Paris group of lawyers.

In Lyon, a store owner, Jean-Christian, said those behind the violence were “animals”. “We saw them looting, men high on adrenaline.” A tourist office in the city centre was set ablaze during the protests amid multiple clashes and looting.

stories.title: Bilawal says KP governor's rule could end if opposition engages with Centre on counterterrorism
summary: PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said on Sunday that if the opposition was willing to fight against terrorism and engage with the Centre on a plan, governor’s rule and emergency imposed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa could end.
His statement comes a week after the Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.
For this reason, he said, the PPP had highlighted the need for a new NAP and consensus on the fight against terrorism, while also extending an invitation to the opposition to play a part in this.

stories.title: Four soldiers dead, dozens injured in fire at Canada military base
summary: Four soldiers were killed and dozens injured in a fire at a military base in Alberta province, one of the worst peacetime tragedies to hit Canada’s armed forces on home soil, Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Sunday.
Prime Minister Mark Carney had posted to X earlier on Saturday that “a serious incident creating a major fire” had occurred at the base.
It’s a one in every 15 to 25-year disaster.” According to the Department of National Defence, the fire broke out around 4pm local time on Saturday (3am PKT on Sunday) in the base’s training area.

stories.title: Prison term should reflect 'crime's gravity'
summary: The Punjab prosecution department has told the Supreme Court that sentences should not routinely run concurrently in every criminal case, including cases involving multiple murders.

The Punjab government maintained that courts should issue reasoned and explicit orders when directing sentences to run consecutively, particularly in exceptional cases involving crimes committed in an exceptionally cruel, barbaric or inhuman manner.

The government argued that automatically ordering concurrent sentences in cases involving multiple victims could diminish the seriousness of additional offences and create an artificial equivalence between killing one person and murdering several.

stories.title: DRAP tightens health product rules
summary: DRAP has issued a new notification bringing eight categories of commonly used health products under stricter regulatory oversight to improve product quality and protect public health.

Under the revised regulatory framework, products covered by the notification will be subject to applicable registration, approval and quality-control requirements before they can be manufactured or marketed in Pakistan.
The move is aimed at ensuring that products carrying medicinal or therapeutic claims meet prescribed quality standards.

stories.title: Western brands feel the pinch amid Chinese economic crunch
summary: With China's economy still struggling to recover from the pandemic, even global fashion icons are beginning to feel the pinch as consumers turn instead to the second-hand market or buy upstart new homegrown brands.
After plunging as much as 19 percent in 2024, mainland China's personal luxury market contracted another three to five percent in 2025, according to consultancy Bain & Company.
China's second-hand luxury market meanwhile exploded 15-20 percent in 2025, according to Bain & Company.

stories.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu in Israeli election
summary: United States President Donald Trump on Sunday endorsed his ally Benjamin Netanyahu as the longtime Israeli prime minister struggles for an edge in next week’s parliamentary election.
Trump praised Netanyahu as a “great warrior prime minster” and peace partner, crediting him with joining the United States in launching strikes on Iran in February.
The election could determine whether Netanyahu remains in power after one of the most consequential periods in Israel’s history, or is defeated by centrist rivals promising to usher in a new era.

stories.title: Smashed storefronts, torched cars and graffiti — France protests and their aftermath in pictures
summary: Torched cars, smashed shopfronts and burnt debris scarred numerous streets in Paris on Sunday, where officials said 557 people were in custody as France reeled from widespread damage caused by violent protests the day before.
Hundreds of shops were looted in Paris and other cities, including Marseille, Bordeaux, Nice and Strasbourg, during the protests over the cost of living.
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 1,800 people were arrested over the protests and looting, with investigations under way “to identify the perpetrators of these acts”.

stories.title: Hidden cost of street politics
summary: According to official estimates compiled by the Ministry of Finance and economic research think tanks, a single day of nationwide disruption, strikes, and capital-bound long marches drains approximately Rs120 billion from national output.

Agricultural wastage (Rs9 billion/day): Perishable agricultural goods – milk, vegetables, poultry and fresh fruit – rot in stranded trucks along provincial highways, inflicting direct capital losses on farmers and sparking localised food inflation in besieged urban centres.

Political actors must establish a cross-party "Charter of the Economy" – a formal consensus that critical infrastructure, digital connectivity, export supply chains and the livelihoods of informal labourers remain off-limits from partisan warfare.

stories.title: Solar is our saviour, capacity charge our drain
summary: The new government in 2013, driven by highly ambitious growth targets and corresponding requirements of power on the grid, launched a new power policy and a massive plan for generation capacity augmentation.

The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra)'s State of the Industry report of 2017 aptly forewarned about the fast-emerging monster of capacity charge due to the increasing gap between generation capacity and consumption.
Solar batteries are also improving this off-grid capacity further by keeping the power available from the same source even after sunset.

stories.title: Was Pakistan ever an open economy?
summary: Pakistan's National Tariff Policy 2025-30 is now in its second year of implementation.
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) similarly identified persistently high tariffs and an increasingly complex tariff structure as important factors behind Pakistan's poor export performance.

Although it is still too early to assess the full impact of the five-year National Tariff Policy, Pakistan's manufacturing sector has recorded growth of more than 6.5% after years of weak performance.

stories.title: A US bond shock will reach Pakistan's doorstep
summary: Officials have told the International Monetary Fund (IMF) that even with oil near $95, average inflation this fiscal year could stay below 9%, keeping real rates comfortably positive, but only if oil holds near $100.

Dollar remittances stretch further when the rupee weakens, and domestic bond yields respond mostly to local inflation and SBP policy, so the pass-through from Washington is partial rather than automatic escalation.

The sell-off in US Treasuries, which has pushed 30-year yields to a 19-year high of 5.36%, will make dollars costlier, narrow SBP's room to manoeuvre and raise the price of fuel that Pakistan cannot produce itself.

stories.title: Customs duty is not the barrier, GST is
summary: One of the underlying objectives of the policy was to stop treating customs tariff as a source of revenue and start treating it as a tool of industrial policy – to provide signals to industry and consumers.
The new tariff policy is gradually reducing overall tariff rates, but it is broadly preserving the cascading.
The industrial policy idea that we should import components, assemble them locally and provide advantage to assemblers by erecting tariff walls on finished goods is deeply flawed.

stories.title: Cairo vows support for Riyadh as 2 Saudi officers killed in helicopter crash near Yemen
summary: Earlier in the day, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said two officers were killed when their helicopter crashed near the Yemen border, after the rebel group claimed it shot the aircraft down.
The incident comes a week after strikes by the Houthis killed 13 people at Riyadh’s international airport, the deadliest attack in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade.
Pakistan, which has signed two defence agreements with Riyadh, has repeatedly expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia.

stories.title: China proposes export controls on solar-manufacturing technologies
summary: China has proposed export controls on 12 technologies used to make solar equipment, citing national security concerns, as part ​of a broader revision that also covers AI and biotechnology.
China would ​ban technologies including ​those used to ⁠make some thin wafers, perovskite and tandem solar cells, as well as large-scale fluidized-bed polysilicon production technologies.
China would also restrict, but not prohibit, exports of advanced solar cell manufacturing technologies, ​including TOPCon, HJT and XBC.

stories.title: Microsoft pulls out of UK data center deal with Nscale, Telegraph reports
summary: Microsoft has pulled out of a data center deal with British cloud ​provider Nscale, Britain's Telegraph newspaper reported on Sunday.
Read: Microsoft plans huge deployment of its own AI chips, with an eye on saving costs The ⁠Telegraph report said Nscale had faced repeated delays with ​the project.
National power grid officials, it reported, had told ​Nscale they did not expect a power supply for the data center until the 2030s.

stories.title: Leaders weigh 'huge benefit', risks of AI for global economy
summary: The artificial intelligence (AI) boom has been a key driver of global growth, but also poses economic risks should investment in the technology falter, experts and policymakers said this week at the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok.
An IMF report released this week projected that a decline in AI investment could reduce global GDP by 0.4 per cent by 2028.
While AI investment and trade have softened the global economic impact of the Middle East war, economists at Moody's Analytics have warned that if the conflict drags on, it could "puncture" the boom.

stories.title: K-P begins process to identify unsafe school buildings across province
summary: He said initial reports had started reaching the relevant authorities, enabling the Education Department to identify potentially hazardous school buildings and take timely action to address safety concerns.
The education adviser also expressed gratitude to citizens who had recorded videos highlighting unsafe school buildings and shared them with the relevant authorities.

He expressed hope that the collective efforts of government officials, education authorities and responsible citizens would contribute to protecting students and staff and ensuring safer conditions in educational institutions across the province.

stories.title: 8 India-sponsored terrorists killed in Quetta, Khuzdar, Nushki districts: ISPR
summary: Security forces have killed eight “India-sponsored” terrorists during three intelligence-based operations conducted in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts of Balochistan, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Sunday.
Separately, during a sanitisation operation in Nushki district, security forces busted a terrorist hideout and “after an intense fire exchange, two India-sponsored terrorists were sent to hell”.
On the night of Oct 12/13, security forces busted a terrorist hideout and killed five terrorists during an IBO in Washuk, ISPR said.

stories.title: Tensions over headscarves, Israel test Azerbaijan-Turkiye ties
summary: The normally close ties between Turkiye and Azerbaijan have come under strain, fuelled by a dispute over Baku’s restrictions on headscarves in schools and disagreements over Israel.

But it also highlighted tensions over the growing rapprochement between Azerbaijan and Israel since Baku’s 2020 Karabakh war with arch-foe Armenia, when the Israelis supplied them with drones and other weaponry.

Turkiye’s ties with Israel, by contrast, could hardly be worse, with Erdogan accusing Israel of genocide in Gaza and Ankara regularly releasing images of top-level talks with the leaders of Hamas, whose October 2023 attacks on Israel sparked the latter’s onslaught on Gaza.

stories.title: Japan to launch historic round-trip mission to Mars moons
summary: Japanese scientists are preparing a mission to Mars’s moons to retrieve samples that could help unlock the origins of the Solar System and life on Earth, in what aims to be the first round trip to the Martian region.
Impact or capture JAXA hopes the mission will reveal how Mars and its two moons formed, a key piece of knowledge in working out how the Solar System was born.
China’s mission US and Chinese space agencies have been racing to be the first to return rock samples from Mars’s surface back to Earth.

stories.title: AI rapidly improving, could vastly boost US GDP, Anthropic's Clark tells policymakers
summary: Clark, speaking at IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, said that international cooperation was needed to erect "unusual and serious rules" for the transformative technology, and there was a shrinking window for policymakers to act.

Clark said that the estimated potential US GDP of $44 trillion, which compares ​to the current level of just over $30 trillion, "sounds very outlandish, I know." But he added that AI was vastly increasing scientific discovery.
Strictest controls ⁠on biological research Clark cautioned that global leaders need to understand how powerful AI will become and make urgent choices about how to regulate the technology.

stories.title: ‘The joke is on us’
summary: For over a month, young people camped at Jantar Mantar – Delhi’s iconic protest site.
In India, young reporters and small digital outlets have covered the protests that big channels ignored.

What is happening in Delhi is less a story about India than a story about the region, about governments that have learned to switch off the internet faster than they can create jobs, and young people who have learned to make jokes faster than governments can ban them.

stories.title: MQM-P calls for new administrative units to address urban Sindh’s woes
summary: At the conclusion of the meeting, MQM-P leaders and legal experts reiterated their commitment to pursuing the party’s demands through political, constitutional and legal means, including advocating new administrative units and reforms to existing laws.

The current debate over new provinces began on July 30, when Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi called for additional administrative units or provinces as part of a broader overhaul of the country’s governance system.

Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah rejected Naqvi’s assessment that the governance system had collapsed and called the proposal outdated, warning that no bloodshed would be allowed over the creation of new provinces.

stories.title: Govt turns to foreign experts to find K2 Airways' black box
summary: Nearly four months after a K2 Airways aircraft plunged into the sea off Ormara, the search for its black box, wreckage and cockpit crew is entering a new phase, with Pakistan stepping up efforts to enlist international expertise for a deep-sea recovery operation.

With the aircraft believed to lie around 3,000 metres below the surface, the search is expected to rely on advanced sonar systems, autonomous underwater vehicles and remotely operated vehicles equipped with high-definition cameras and specialised recovery tools.
The technology can map underwater terrain, measure depths and identify potential obstructions, helping search teams narrow down the area where the aircraft’s wreckage may be located.

stories.title: Maldives President Muizzu to visit Pakistan from Oct 20-22: FO
summary: Maldives’ President Dr Mohamed Muizzu will undertake a three-day state visit to Pakistan from Oct 20-22 at the invitation of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Sunday.
The forthcoming visit reflected the “shared commitment of both countries to further strengthening their bilateral partnership and opening new avenues of mutually beneficial cooperation”, it added.
In 2015, former Maldivian president Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom undertook a two-day state visit to Pakistan on May 6-7 at the invitation of then-premier Nawaz Sharif.

stories.title: My father survived the Karsaz bombing; each new terror attack takes us back there
summary: My father had found his way to an ambulance that was taking him to the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre — a designated hospital for injuries and casualties — but he eventually ended up at (what is now known as) the Dr Ruth Pfau Civil Hospital Karachi.
Had any patient in his condition come to the hospital that night, they would have been surgically operated on by my father and his team.
Some among us are still able to deal with terrorism using the standard emotional survival process mentioned at the beginning of this piece.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz inaugurates Daanish School in Islamabad, stresses equal academic opportunities
summary: Daanish schools, originally introduced by the Punjab government, aim to provide quality education to marginalised and talented students.
Education Minister Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui also spoke on the occasion.
In March, thousands of students across Pakistan sought admission to the school, which received over 7,000 applications against just 210 seats.

stories.title: First Pakistani astronaut to undertake space mission from China on Nov 25: Ahsan Iqbal
summary: Pakistan’s first astronaut will undertake a space mission from a Chinese space centre on November 25, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said on Sunday.

The minister made the announcement while addressing the concluding ceremony of World Space Week in Narowal, held in collaboration with the Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (Suparco), the planning ministry said in a statement.

According to the handout, the planning minister also said the country was aiming to achieve a lunar landing by 2035, expressing hope that Pakistan’s cooperation with China would help it “reach new heights in space exploration”.

stories.title: 'France is burning', Trump blames immigration for riots
summary: US President Donald Trump on Sunday blamed immigration for the widespread rioting that erupted in cities across France, stating that France was "burning", further urging authorities to "take control" and close borders.
In a Truth Social post on Sunday, Trump wrote that "France is burning!", accusing immigrants of "shattering a once great country".
In a post on X, Vance said that “Western liberals imported the third world into France and other countries in the name of diversity and compassion.

stories.title: Wasim Akram advises over-50s to limit WhatsApp, social media use
summary: Former Pakistan cricket captain Wasim Akram has shared a humorous message for people aged over 50, offering advice on how to use mobile phones, WhatsApp and social media without overwhelming others with messages and calls.
Sharing the video on Instagram, Akram wrote, “Viewer discretion: THIS VIDEO IS AVAILABLE FOR PEOPLE OVER 50 ON HOW AND WHEN TO USE A MOBILE PHONE/ WHATSAPP.
He added that people should not feel obliged to send good morning messages to everyone daily.

stories.title: Quetta chamber urges traders to reject 'negative propaganda' amid Iran border closure
summary: The Quetta Chamber of Commerce and Industry on Sunday urged traders and people affected by the closure of the Pakistan-Iran border not to believe any “negative propaganda”, expressing hope that the situation would improve soon.
The chamber urged all traders and people affected by the border closures to remain hopeful that the situation would improve soon and not to believe any “baseless negative propaganda” in this regard.
The border closure coincided with regulatory developments from the Ministry of Commerce.

stories.title: Musk back in the spotlight, but politics dims the awe
summary: Now Musk is back in Trump’s good graces, after a spectacular falling-out that followed his exit from DOGE in May 2025.
Last week, Trump presented Musk with the nation’s top science medal, calling him a “national treasure” and “our modern-day Thomas Edison”.
The same may be true of Musk’s dealings with Washington.

stories.title: Khawaja Asif raises alarm over bureaucrats' 'exodus' to Portugal
summary: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Sunday questioned the commitment of senior bureaucrats to Pakistan, alleging that a significant number of government officers had planned to settle abroad while still serving the country.

In a statement on X, Asif said that while Pakistan’s bureaucracy had capable and honest officers, many officials had made Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom and other European countries their permanent homes over the past several years.

Questioning the commitment of senior officials who had occupied high offices and enjoyed the privileges and respect associated with public service, Asif asked whether their loyalty to Pakistan remained beyond suspicion throughout their careers.

stories.title: Pope Leo pledges gradual return to duties in first event since cancer surgery
summary: Pope Leo pledged on Sunday ​to slowly resume his usual activities as the leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics as he ‌greeted crowds in St Peter's Square during his first public event since undergoing surgery for lung cancer five days ago.
Read: Pope Leo returns to Vatican four days after lung cancer surgery "Having overcome this delicate phase...

Pope's calendar in flux Leo usually keeps a busy schedule, but the Vatican has cancelled his other public events until at least Wednesday, when he is due to hold ​a weekly general audience in St Peter's Square.

stories.title: Pakistan suspends Iran trade corridors over 'security, smuggling concerns'
summary: GWADAR/QUETTA: Pakistan has suspended trade with Iran through the official Gabd-Rimdan (250) and Taftan border crossings, it emerged on Saturday.

Shahid Rind, adviser to the Balochistan chief minister on media and political affairs, said the “purpose of the temporary closure of the Pak-Iran border is to address security concerns, prevent smuggling, and make the border system more effective”.
The visit came a couple of months after it was reported that trade between Pakistan and Iran through the Gabd-Rimdan border crossing had come to a complete halt.
